daily.title: Nigeria detains 5 Mexicans, confiscates over $220 million of meth
daily.summary: Nigeria's anti-drug agency said Mexican experts were allegedly recruited by a Nigerian national to run a meth laboratory in the southeastern state of Enugu.

daily.title: Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era
daily.summary: After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's Kremlin-friendly former PM Viktor Orban, his successor, Peter Magyar, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy seek to reset their countries' ties.

daily.title: Spain: Canary Islands witness 1-day migration record
daily.summary: The arrival of over 2,000 migrants to the islands comes as Spain holds elections this weekend. The president of the Canary Islands said the archipelago is facing "unprecedented migration pressure."

daily.title: €561 Billion and Still Not Enough: Germany's 2027 Budget Exposes a Coalition on the Brink
daily.summary: The budget for 2027 has reached new highs, and pension funds, defense spending and a weak economy are increasing the pressure. At the same time, tensions are mounting within the government.

daily.title: US Army detonates unstable lead-based explosives in Iowa
daily.summary: The US Army says a controlled blast is the safest way to deal with explosive chemicals that began crystallizing in storage. US President Donald Trump said "mitigation efforts have far exceeded expectations."

daily.title: EU must set out a new timeline for cage-free farming, court rules
daily.summary: European General Court ruled that the European Commission has failed to set out a timeline after pledging to end caged farming by the end of 2023.

daily.title: Nigeria's upcoming election marred by rising AI disinformation
daily.summary: As Nigeria inches closer to the 2027 polls, the use of artificial intelligence in the electoral process has prompted questions about integrity and institutional readiness. Can Nigerians trust their democratic processes?

daily.title: Ukraine: Poland to set up no-fly zone near Ukraine border
daily.summary: Poland urged NATO allies to be vigilant at their borders after repeated Russian airspace incursions. Allies have also offered different opinions on Kyiv attacking Russian ships in Libya. Follow DW for the latest.

daily.title: US plans new tariffs on EU, China and 12 others
daily.summary: The Trump administration is planning new import duties of up to 20% to counter excessive manufacturing abroad. The measures could put further pressure on US consumers already struggling with high living costs.

daily.title: German firms eye Africa as global trade shocks hit traditional markets
daily.summary: German businesses are optimistic about Africa, but Berlin's cautious approach to risk is holding them back from cashing in on the opportunities that their competitors from countries like the UAE and Turkey are seizing.

daily.title: EU plans €50 billion sovereign tech equity fund to boost quantum technology
daily.summary: The European Commission proposed a tech fund with a target size of €50 billion to boost quantum computing efforts. The bloc aims to keep up with the US and China in the global race.

daily.title: Ice hockey prospect Max Calce follows Leon Draisaitl's path, leaving Mannheim for Canada
daily.summary: The player widely seen as Germany's biggest ice hockey talent to come along in years is leaving the country's top professional league for Canada – changing tracks in his bid to make it to the NHL.

daily.title: Why Indian nationals are still ending up in Russia's war on Ukraine
daily.summary: Whether through deception or desperation, Indians continue to be drawn into Russia's war in Ukraine. What can New Delhi do to protect its citizens from ending up fighting in Ukraine?

daily.title: In Afghanistan, no female doctor often means no treatment for women
daily.summary: Millions of women in Afghanistan, particularly pregnant women, are suffering under Taliban restrictions and are increasingly losing access to life-saving medical care.

daily.title: Spain: Catalan separatist Puigdemont sets date for return
daily.summary: Former Catalan leader Carles Puigdemont plans to return to Barcelona on December 12 after nearly a decade in exile. Spain's Supreme Court has dropped the criminal case against him, clearing the way for his return.

daily.title: North Korea expels Swiss envoy over sanctions on camp accused of indoctrinating Ukrainian children
daily.summary: North Korea has ordered Switzerland to close its newly reopened diplomatic office. The dispute centers on Swiss sanctions against a camp accused of indoctrinating Ukrainian children from Russian-occupied territories.

daily.title: Australia, Solomon Islands sign sweeping pact seen as countering China
daily.summary: Australia will become the Solomon Islands' primary security partner, while the archipelago will reject any foreign power trying to "interfere" on its "sensitive" infrastructure.

daily.title: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi refinery, financial district
daily.summary: Iran-backed Yemeni Houthis say they carried out fresh retaliatory attacks in Saudi Arabia. A fire was reported at Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh's financial district was attacked for the second time in a week.

daily.title: Fact check: Deepfakes and 'US abandons Taiwan' claims spread ahead of vote
daily.summary: Ahead of local elections, Taiwan is seeing a surge in AI-generated attacks on mayoral candidate Puma Shen, alongside disinformation portraying the US as abandoning the island.

daily.title: Climate loss and damage fund exists, but the money doesn't
daily.summary: Climate-vulnerable countries fought for years to create a loss and damage fund. Four years on, demand far outstrips funding, pledges are scarce, and disaster-hit nations are still waiting for support.

daily.title: Germany's women's football team take stand against domestic violence
daily.summary: Germany's women's football team are to wear UN Women badges in games against Argentina and Peru, as domestic violence hits a record high in Germany.

daily.title: German auto workers on back foot as costs, competition bite
daily.summary: German auto workers profited during the industry's boom years, but are now increasingly being asked to trade past gains for future job security.

daily.title: Domestic violence soars to record high in Germany
daily.summary: Every three days in Germany, a man kills his wife or ex-partner. Every 10 minutes, the police record a sexual offense against a woman. "A shocking finding," according to Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig.

weekly.title: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
weekly.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

weekly.title: EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
weekly.summary: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.

weekly.title: CAS reinstates Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions
weekly.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions, overturning a CAF decision that stripped them of the title. Morocco, previously declared winners, are confirmed runners-up.

weekly.title: Bombed factories, billion-dollar opportunity: Why German companies are staying in Ukraine
weekly.summary: German companies remain committed to Ukraine despite million-dollar losses, an unreliable energy supply and a shortage of skilled workers. They are betting on new markets and long-term growth.

weekly.title: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble
weekly.summary: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.

weekly.title: German directors' doc on stolen film wins International Emmy Award
weekly.summary: Two German film students confronted the American who won festival prizes with their animated movie. "The Talented Mr. F," their documentary on their fight against plagiarism, is now in the spotlight.

weekly.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
weekly.summary: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.

weekly.title: Weapons, war and wavering trust: Germans want to see more restraint in foreign policy
weekly.summary: According to a study by the Körber Foundation, a growing number of Germans now oppose providing military aid to Ukraine. The majority also believes that Germany should take a neutral position between the US and China.

weekly.title: US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035
weekly.summary: FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host the 2031 Women's World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams. The UK will stage the 2035 edition, its first World Cup since 1966.

weekly.title: Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
weekly.summary: As the World Chess championship gets underway, it's no coincidence that the titleholder, Gukesh Dommaraju, and his challenger, Jakhovir Sindarov, are both from Asia.

weekly.title: Nvidia reinstates former CEO Jensen Huang despite China espionage scandal
weekly.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back the disgraced CEO, who resigned this month amid news of his affairs. He's suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset.

weekly.title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
weekly.summary: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.

weekly.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
weekly.summary: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

weekly.title: COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy
weekly.summary: COP31 has been branded a failure after countries couldn't reach a final agreement, divided over a reference to "fossil fuels." But was the decision to walk away from a watered-down text actually a show of strength?

weekly.title: German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
weekly.summary: Police in Germany are responding to bomb threats against a series of schools, but say that at present they don't believe them to be credible. Danish authorities are reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.

weekly.title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
weekly.summary: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.

weekly.title: Budget cuts threaten Germany's fight against antisemitism and racism
weekly.summary: Numerous grassroots initiatives in Germany are facing funding cuts. Affected organizations are sounding the alarm, pointing to growing challenges posed by far-right extremism.

weekly.title: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect
weekly.summary: A new project and exhibition, "The Night Watch Lives," lifts the veil on the hidden world of microbes covering one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.

weekly.title: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
weekly.summary: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.

weekly.title: Germany news: Metalworkers go on strike as pay dispute heats up
weekly.summary: Germany's biggest union is calling for more strikes over heated pay disputes with car makers like Mercedes and shipyards among the companies impacted. Meanwhile, a Berlin hospital fire leaves many injured.

weekly.title: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help
weekly.summary: Seeing someone break a rule makes people more likely to break it too, a new study finds, especially when the rule-breaker is on their side politically. Watching others behave well barely made a difference.

weekly.title: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use
weekly.summary: After two weeks of tough talks, the COP31 climate summit has closed without a consensus on how to quit fossil fuels or fund countries struggling to adapt to a hotter world.

weekly.title: Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029
weekly.summary: "The Goodforces" wants to see a swing to the left in the 2029 German elections. The agency counts New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Bernie Sanders among its inspirations. Could it transform the political landscape?

weekly.title: Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
weekly.summary: Germany's biggest single union, IG Metall, is calling on car and shipyard workers to strike amid a pay row. Meanwhile, Germany's president is setting off on an Africa trip. DW has more.

weekly.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
weekly.summary: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.

weekly.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
weekly.summary: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

weekly.title: EU takes aim at tech giants in tax proposal
weekly.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

weekly.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
weekly.summary: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

weekly.title: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad
weekly.summary: Harassment, persecution, surveillance: Across much of the world, people of faith are facing growing pressure. A new German government report is unusually direct in criticizing China in particular.

weekly.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
weekly.summary: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.

weekly.title: COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading
weekly.summary: Attacks on climate science and disinformation risk delaying key measures at COP31 in Antalya. As the UN climate talks draw to a close, how will that affect efforts to come to an agreement?

weekly.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
weekly.summary: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

weekly.title: Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future
weekly.summary: Never before have young people around the world been so well-educated while facing so many economic challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents?

weekly.title: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience
weekly.summary: The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years ago.

weekly.title: Germany face Belgium in Nations League quarterfinals — Klopp plays down favorites tag
weekly.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is looking to "carry positive momentum forward" as his team draw neighboring Belgium in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League.

weekly.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
weekly.summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

weekly.title: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
weekly.summary: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.

weekly.title: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?
weekly.summary: Two challengers to Gianni Infantino have registered for next year's FIFA presidential election. What do Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima stand for – and do they stand a chance against the incumbent?

weekly.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports
weekly.summary: According to a letter obtained by the media, Lufthansa's executive board said the German company is losing €20 million every month. In addition to job cuts, operational cuts are also planned.

weekly.title: Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?
weekly.summary: From record-breaking heat to devastating floods and wildfires, the warning signs are everywhere. Can rising temperatures still be brought under control?

weekly.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
weekly.summary: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

weekly.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
weekly.summary: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.

weekly.title: Anthropic trading tests investors' appetite for AI
weekly.summary: Anthropic was valued at $2 trillion after shares started trading on the Nasdaq following a record $81 billion IPO. Its performance will put investor confidence in AI to the test.

weekly.title: Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend
weekly.summary: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev is facing a new lawsuit related to a domestic abuse trial. The lawyer for his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, told DW what the allegations are against the German player.

weekly.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
weekly.summary: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

weekly.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
weekly.summary: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

weekly.title: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
weekly.summary: As Donald Trump seeks to tighten economic pressure on Iran, China remains its biggest oil customer and Russia a key partner. But both powers are balancing support for Tehran against broader interests with Washington.

weekly.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
weekly.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.
